title: Canonical finite ordinary sections comparison and adjunction pullback
statement:
Let $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ be the datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $Y\to s$ be any scheme over $k$. Use the intrinsic constant-ring module realization of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], the exact point sections $\Gamma_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and the ordinary derived direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Define $F_Y=\Gamma_s\circ Ra_{Y*}$, the ambient functor whose values at $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ are exactly finiteOrdinarySections of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], and $G_Y=R\Gamma_{\mathrm{abs}}(Y,-)$ using [lem-trf-proetale-unit-leray-chain-formula], in the same coefficient-derived-category universe as $F_Y$. The point-section comparison with realization-inverse terminal evaluation is the unique natural isomorphism sending the scalar-unit realization of each section of each fixed-scalar sheaf back to that section after the realization unit inverse. Compose it with inverse terminal evaluation to identify point sections with absolute sections on $s$. Define $c_Y:F_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}G_Y$ by the canonical exact-postcomposition derived comparison, that point identification and the $a_Y$ terminal/Leray identification. Thus $c_Y$ is the canonical $a_Y$ Leray plus point-sections comparison, not an arbitrary natural isomorphism.

For any scheme endomorphism $h:Y\to Y$, with no assumption that it is over $s$, let $t_h:G_Y Rh_*\xrightarrow{\sim}G_Y$ be the canonical terminal/Leray comparison of [lem-trf-proetale-unit-leray-chain-formula]. Transport $t_h$ through $c_Y$ to define $\lambda_h:F_Y Rh_*\xrightarrow{\sim}F_Y$. With the derived adjunction of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and [def-weil-derived-direct-image], define $\rho^F_{h,M}=\lambda_{h,Lh^*M}\circ F_Y(\eta_{h,M})$. This is ordinary pullback on the recorded point-fibre/direct-image model. Its compatibility with the absolute unit pullback is
$$c_{Y,Lh^*M}\circ\rho^F_{h,M}=t_{h,Lh^*M}\circ G_Y(\eta_{h,M})\circ c_{Y,M}$$
for every derived object $M$, naturally in $M$ and for every $h$; in particular it holds for $h=\Phi_Y^m$ and $h=g_Y^m$ of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius].
